items.title: Louis Nelson Interview, 1960-04-18
items.q: INTERVIEWER: You played with Kid Rene too then? I did, yeah, yes. ... INTERVIEWER: Who else was in Kid Rene's band on that job, can you remember? INTERVIEWEE: Oh, myself, Rene, probably they call it Sport, that's Young.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, he was a powerful fellow. Yeah, a powerful fellow. You see in those times they used to call you, when you give a dance, like if you'd give a dance, like if it's going to be Saturday night, or Saturday in the day they'd call and make an advertisement. You'd get on the truck or the wagon, whatever it was, you understand, and go around and play. And when Buddy Petit and Rene would meet, that's it. Yeah, yeah, yeah, they'd go see who can out-blow each other. That was it right there. Surely.
You played with Kid Rene too then? I did, yeah, yes.
He was playing at the Levita. Yeah, he used to play at the Levita, the Levita dance hall. How was he?

items.title: Louis Nelson Interview, 1960-04-18
items.q: how does it compare with the other bands you play with such as, you know, like Buddy Petit or Kid Renee or Chris Kelly?

ctx.x: I just wondered how Buddy Petit and Kid Renee compared with Louis?

Well to my judgment Buddy Petit was about, after Louis left here, he was about the best trumpet player around here. He was really good. He was a good jazz man. Buddy Petit was wonderful. To my opinion, maybe somebody might think differently. A lot of people told us that. Some of them, you know, I don't know. People have told us that. He was a little short fellow used to wear, wearing them stiff rimmed straw hats in the summertime and a brown derby in the wintertime. Yeah. Did he use his derby ever over the bell?…
